articles.title: AICWA seeks intervention from PM Narendra Modi regarding the security concerns in Bollywood after Amitabh Bachchan's recent appearance with a bulletproof glass post gun fire on Tiger Shroff
articles.summary: Amitabh Bachchan's recent appearance outside his Juhu residence, Jalsa, with bulletproof glass separating him from the crowd has sparked concern across
articles.body: Amitabh Bachchan's recent appearance outside his Juhu residence, Jalsa, with bulletproof glass separating him from the crowd has sparked concern across the film industry. The actor has followed the tradition of greeting fans outside his home every Sunday for decades. However, his November 1 appearance was markedly different, with the 84-year-old stepping out behind a protective glass shield. His son Abhishek Bachchan was by his side, keeping an eye on the crowd. The incident has now drawn attention to the growing security concerns surrounding Bollywood, with the All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) approaching Prime Minister Narendra Modi and seeking urgent intervention to protect members of the film fraternity.In a letter dated November 3, 2026, AICWA president Suresh Shyam Lal Gupta urged the Prime Minister to take immediate steps to strengthen security for actors, filmmakers and their families. The association highlighted several incidents of shootings, physical attacks and extortion threats involving film personalities, stating that the situation calls for serious attention.The association also referred to Bachchan's long-standing Sunday ritual, when fans from different parts of India and abroad gather outside Jalsa to catch a glimpse of the actor. His son, Abhishek Bachchan, accompanied him during the November 1 appearance. Expressing concern over the circumstances that led the veteran actor to take such precautions while meeting his admirers, the letter stated, “For more than four decades he has met his fans there every Sunday, and people from across India and abroad come just to see him. At the age of 84, he never imagined he would have to protect himself like this in his own city. His son Abhishek Bachchan, who rarely comes out, stood beside him to protect his father.”The association further described the sight as unprecedented, saying it had left the film fraternity deeply disturbed. It wrote, “People have heard of bulletproof cars. Never before had they seen a superstar step out of his home behind bulletproof glass just to meet the people who love him. This image will be remembered in the history of Indian cinema, and the whole industry was shaken by it.”In its appeal to the Prime Minister, the association listed several incidents involving prominent members of the entertainment industry. These include the murder of Baba Siddique in Bandra, the firing outside Salman Khan's residence, the knife attack on Saif Ali Khan at his home and the shooting outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty's Juhu residence.The letter also referred to multiple firing incidents targeting comedian Kapil Sharma's cafe in Canada, along with the recent shooting incident involving Tiger Shroff in Juhu. The association expressed particular concern about the latter, pointing out that the incident took place in a busy neighbourhood with several people present.Highlighting the seriousness of the attack, the letter stated, “Tiger Shroff was fired upon in Juhu, one of Mumbai's most prominent VIP areas, in the presence of a large crowd. Two persons were hit by bullets... Tiger Shroff has no known controversy and no known enmity with anyone. He was targeted in broad daylight for one reason: to spread terror.”The association has suggested that extortion could be a common motive behind several of these incidents. According to the letter, criminal gangs are increasingly targeting Bollywood personalities because of the industry's prominence and international visibility. It alleged that attacks on well-known actors and filmmakers are being used to spread fear, gain notoriety and extract large sums of money. The letter also mentioned reports of Tusshar Kapoor allegedly receiving an extortion demand of Rs 5 crore.Explaining its position, the AICWA stated, “All these attacks appear to be aimed at extortion. Gangsters know that Bollywood is the softest target and that it is known all over the world. By attacking famous film personalities, they want to make a name for themselves and to extort money on a large scale.”Beyond the safety of film personalities, the AICWA has questioned the broader law-and-order situation in Mumbai. It argued that if high-profile individuals are vulnerable to such attacks, the safety of ordinary residents is also at stake. Calling for concrete security measures rather than assurances, the association stated, “Today, law and order has broken down in Mumbai. If a celebrity like Tiger Shroff is not safe in the heart of the city, an ordinary Mumbaikar cannot feel safe either. In 2026, the terror of the underworld, which was believed to have been brought under control, has returned to the streets of Mumbai. Words alone are not enough; Bollywood needs real and visible protection.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.body: A special Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) court in Mumbai on Tuesday sent Suneha Pandit, the 13th accused in the firing incident targeting actor Tiger Shroff, to police custody till November 16. She is the sister-in-law of gangster Anil Pandit, who had claimed responsibility for the October 18 firing.Suneha Pandit arrested in Karnal in Tiger Shroff firing caseAccording to the IANS report, the Mumbai Crime Branch arrested Suneha Pandit from Haryana’s Karnal district. She was presented before the special MCOCA court on Tuesday, where investigators asked for her custody for further questioning. The police had sought 15 days of custody.Cryptocurrency account under the scannerOfficials said Suneha Pandit is the wife of Abhishek, who allegedly operates a cryptocurrency account. Money has reportedly come into this account from abroad, and investigators suspect it may be proceeds of extortion.Abhishek Pandit is the brother of Anil Pandit. He is accused of running two other groups along with his own network and is said to handle payments for all operations. Police said the other accused in the case were given special codes, which Abhishek allegedly used to transfer money to them.Defence opposes custodySuneha Pandit’s lawyer opposed the custody request, arguing that the police have already obtained all the information they needed. The Crime Branch, however, told the court that the funds allegedly used in the Tiger Shroff firing case came from foreign sources. The court then sent her to the custody of the Mumbai Crime Branch until November 16.Earlier arrests in the caseLast week, a special MCOCA court sent Amar, the 12th accused, to police custody till November 6. He was arrested in Rohna village in Haryana’s Sonipat. Officials said he allegedly transferred money online that was used in the crime, including for buying a motorcycle and booking hotel rooms linked to the case.Before that, the court had sent 11 other accused arrested in connection with the firing on Shroff’s car to police custody till November 6.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Mandya DC Kumara directs officials to identify minority community school dropouts working in garages and bring them back to education under PM’s 15-point programme.

articles.title: Ian McKellen pays emotional tribute to Patrick Stewart at a gala in London with a song from their ‘Waiting for Godot’ days: 'Let’s remember Pat Stewart, a great actor'
articles.summary: Veteran actor Ian McKellen paid a touching musical tribute to his close friend Patrick Stewart at a charity gala in London.
articles.body: Veteran actor Ian McKellen paid a touching musical tribute to his close friend Patrick Stewart at a charity gala in London. He led the audience in a song that the two actors once performed together on stage. The late actor, loved for playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in ‘Star Trek’ and Professor Charles Xavier in the ‘X-Men’ films, died at his Los Angeles home on October 28. He was 86.Ian McKellen sings in Patrick Stewart’s memoryIan Mckellen's tribute came at the Raise the Roof! gala at London’s Victoria Palace Theatre, days after he had shared an emotional Instagram post about Patrick Stewart. The event raised funds for the GBP 26 million Centenary Appeal for Denville Hall, a home for retired entertainment professionals. Patrick Stewart was an ambassador for the organisation.Dressed in a dark suit and a bright yellow scarf, Ian Mckellen walked on stage and spoke to the audience without a microphone. He then invited everyone to sing ‘Underneath the Arches’, a 1932 music-hall song made popular by Bud Flanagan and Chesney Allen.The song held a special place in the friendship between the two actors. Before starting, Ian Mckellen asked the audience to think of Patrick Stewart as they sang. He said, “When we played the tramps in Samuel Beckett’s Waiting for Godot, Pat Stewart and I sang that song – here in London and on Broadway – at the end of the show. And we’re going to sing it now for you; I hope you enjoy. Now I’ve reminded you of some of the words. As we sing it, let’s remember Pat Stewart, a great actor.”A video of the moment is now going around on social media, and many fans have said they were moved by the personal memory behind it.A friendship beyond the fameIn his long Instagram tribute, Ian remembered the man behind the famous roles. He wrote about Patrick’s deep love for Yorkshire, his frank and outspoken nature, and how he stayed connected to his roots even after spending most of his life in America.Ian also recalled a conversation on a London street, when Patrick told him he had been offered a lead role in ‘Star Trek’. Ian worried that taking it could keep his friend away from the British stage for years. He wrote, “But Patrick, think of your stage career in the UK. Do you really want to risk—getting lost in Hollywood for years and years?”Their bond also shaped their work. Audiences across the world loved them as Magneto and Professor X in the ‘X-Men’ films, where their characters stood on opposite sides of an ideological divide. The two also shared the Broadway stage in ‘No Man’s Land’ and ‘Waiting for Godot’.Patrick Stewart’s death confirmedHis spokesperson confirmed the news a day later and revealed that the actor had been battling Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.Patrick Stewart’s final filmPatrick Stewart is set to return as Professor Charles Xavier for the last time in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’. Marvel Studios has confirmed that the December release will mark the veteran actor’s final appearance as the iconic character. This means fans will not see him as Xavier in the 2027 sequel, ‘Avengers: Secret Wars’.‘Avengers: Doomsday’ will release in Indian theatres on December 17, a day before its US release. articles.title: Nicolas Cage says he’s ‘a little bit homeless’ as sinkhole swallows his Malibu home
articles.summary: Nicolas Cage said he is “a little bit homeless” thanks to a sinkhole that has consumed a part of his Malibu home.
articles.body: Nicolas Cage said he is “a little bit homeless” thanks to a sinkhole that has consumed a part of his Malibu home. Talking about his Halloween plans at a Los Angeles Comic Con panel over the weekend, Cage said he is “currently a little bit homeless.” “Something happened in my house in Malibu. So, I’m just sort of living in hotels, so I don’t have the normal trick-or-treaters I would like to enjoy tonight,” he said, according to a fan video of the panel. A huge sinkhole formed in the driveway of Cage’s home on the Southern California coast in September. At the time, authorities were investigating what caused the sinkhole to open up. City officials said the sinkhole had also caused a gas leak, but no one was hurt. Video of the home shows a massive crater in the driveway that appeared to swallow up everything that was sitting on top. It was not clear from aerial imaging whether the house itself sustained any damage. According to an emergency proclamation from the City of Malibu, the sinkhole started to form on Sept. 7, and fully emerged on Sept. 8, measuring 25-30 feet deep and 30 by 60 feet wide. Seven homes were “red-tagged” due to hazardous conditions brought on by the sinkhole, the proclamation said, as were an additional 24 homes “due to the loss of safe vehicular access.” Gas services in the area were shut off. The next day, the city said the housing association that controls the area would be working on repairs. It said repairs were expected to be completed within five weeks “depending on conditions.” Representatives for Cage did not immediately respond to an NBC News request for comment. It was not clear how long he has been out of the home and when he will be able to return. The City of Malibu has not released any further information about the sinkhole, and did not immediately respond to a request for more information.

articles.title: Bruce Springsteen sparks fan fury after backing Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan Senate race
articles.summary: Bruce Springsteen's endorsement of Abdul El-Sayed in the Michigan Senate race drew fierce backlash from fans citing antisemitism concerns.
articles.body: Bruce Springsteen has a message for Michigan voters — and some of his longtime fans aren't having it. The rock legend faced criticism from some social media users after backing Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, prompting angry fans to accuse The Boss of crossing a political line. Springsteen, who has never shied away from politics, took aim at President Donald Trump in his endorsement of El-Sayed, portraying the progressive candidate as a defender of American democracy. "Dr. El-Sayed is a fighter for our American Constitution, he’s a fighter for our American Democracy, and he’s a fighter against the corrupt, lawless, and anti-American leadership currently in the White House. That’s why I’m in his corner 100%. Bruce Springsteen," he penned on social media. "Bruce Springsteen, the guy who spent 40 years cashing in on ‘Born in the USA,’ finally posts after two years of silence just to call an elected American president ‘corrupt, lawless, and anti-American’ while locking arms with Abdul El-Sayed, the same guy who campaigned with Hasan Piker (the streamer who said America deserved 9/11) and still can’t shake the Muslim Brotherhood questions about his own family." You are acting like an ignorant uneducated school child. You did this for what reason? This is so foolish. I’m so sad., I’m 59 years old.. Shame on me for thinking you were educated and smarter. Take the time to understand the other point of view." However, not everyone was ready to turn on the rock icon. articles.title: Cuatro profesores irrumpen por sorpresa en el programa de Christian Gálvez y el presentador estalla: "Este no es vuestro espacio"
articles.standfirst: El televisivo tuvo que dar paso a publicidad tras este momento
articles.summary: El televisivo tuvo que dar paso a publicidad tras este momento
articles.body: En las últimas semanas, algunas manifestaciones en clave educativa y de vivienda se han vivido por las calles de Madrid. Pues bien, en la tarde de este martes, 3 de noviembre, en el programa de ‘La tarde de Telemadrid’, presentado por Christian Gálvez en el citado canal autonómico, ha ocurrido algo inesperado cuando iba a tener un debate con varios tertulianos sobre si era mejor ducharse por la mañana o por la noche. De repente, cuatro profesores (dos chicos y cuatros chicas) que se encontraban con el público saltaron al plató con camisetas verdes en la que reivindican que la escuela pública es de todos y para todos. Gálvez reaccionó al instante, afeando el comportamiento de los docentes. Estas personas reivindicaron los derechos de los profesionales del sector y el presentador intervino al respecto: “Gracias, chicos, pero las artes que habéis utilizado para hacer esto no me parecen las correctas, no son las pertinentes y no son las que los docentes por los que yo he aplaudido y peleado toda la vida utilizarían”. Sin embargo, Christian Gálvez defendió la escuela pública, desvelando que él antes de dedicarse al mundo del periodismo, tenía gusto por la docencia: “Yo no iba a ser presentador de televisión, iba a ser profesor. Adoro la enseñanza pública. Muchísimas gracias, pero creo que ahora mismo este no es vuestro espacio”. “Lo siento. Tengo la enorme fortuna de haber podido elegir una carrera como magisterio, educación primaria. Carrera que nunca llegué a terminar porque el tren de la televisión pasó por delante. Un tren de esos que se aprovechan una sola vez en la vida. Afortunadamente nunca jamás en mi vida, y no digo que tengan razón o que no, un profesor me engañó como me han engañado ellos”, sentenció antes de dar paso a publicidad.

articles.title: Pierce Brosnan Has High Praise for ‘Strong’ James Bond Contender Callum Turner
articles.summary: Turner is reportedly among the final candidates to become the next 007 in Denis Villeneuve’s upcoming film about the iconic spy
articles.body:
Pierce Brosnan, like pretty much everyone else on the planet, is "eager" to see who will be cast as the next James Bond. He admitted, however, that he has a bit of a soft spot for one of the frontrunners: Callum Turner.

As TheWrap reported last month , four actors made it to the final round of screen tests. According to insiders, Turner, "Slow Horses" breakout Jack Lowden and Josh O'Connor were among those tested, along with an unknown actor, for the role of the next 007 for Amazon.

"All the men who are on the list now are actors I admire," the former Bond actor told Vanity Fair in an interview published Tuesday. "Callum Turner is someone I've worked with, and he's so strong." Although he's a fan of Turner, Brosnan said he thinks any of the actors left in the running would do a great job as the iconic spy.

"They all have a voice and a physique, and a presence on film," he shared. "They all have longevity as actors, all of these young men. Whoever plays the role, I wish him the very best of life and strength and courage. It's hard to tell who it would be, but I eagerly await to hear the news and the celebration of the next James Bond."

Brosnan may be the only former Bond to comment on the next 007 thus far, but he's not the only former co-star to weigh in. Gary Oldman, who stars in Apple TV's "Slow Horses" alongside Lowden, told Canada's Global News in a September interview that the next James Bond had already been chosen and that he hoped it was Lowden.

"It's been rumored that he's on the shortlist," he said at the time. "We're going to find out pretty soon, aren't we? Because they have picked him. They have made their choice, but they have not announced it yet. So my fingers are crossed for Jack."

The next Bond movie will be the first installment since longtime stewards Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson ceded full creative control of the franchise to the studio. Oscar-nominated "Dune" filmmaker Denis Villeneuve is set to direct the first new film in the franchise since Daniel Craig's farewell in 2021's "No Time to Die." Amazon MGM Studios hired "Peaky Blinders" creator Steven Knight to write the screenplay for the 26th James Bond film.

Amazon MGM selected Amy Pascal and David Heyman as the new producers of the Bond series after talks with Broccoli and Wilson over its future stalled. The two ceded creative control but remain co-owners of the franchise.

articles.title: Nicole Taylor of country music trio Taylor Red dies at 35
articles.summary: The singer died on Sept. 28 after a battle with breast cancer, her sisters said.
articles.body:
Nicole Taylor, one-third of the country music group Taylor Red, has died, according to a statement from her sisters shared on the group's official website. She was 35.

According to the statement , Nicole Taylor died Sept. 28, 2026. A private funeral service was held by her family.

Nicole Taylor, who was a member of Taylor Red with her triplet sisters Nika and Natalie Taylor, was diagnosed with an aggressive form of breast cancer in 2022, her sisters said in an Instagram video shared Monday.

In the video, Nika and Natalie Taylor said their older sister battled cancer "fearlessly" and told her loved ones "We're not going to live in dread during all of this."

"She even did CrossFit while she was doing her [chemotherapy] treatments," Nika Taylor said.

According to the sisters, Nicole Taylor initially "responded well to [chemotherapy] treatments" and had been declared "evidence without disease," but was later told her cancer had progressed to Stage 4.

Despite doctors giving her three months to live after that diagnosis, her sisters said she went on to live for another year.

"She tried not to live in fear, remained really hopeful, traveled, she tried to live life, she worked really hard, she tried to have fun," Natalie Taylor said.

According to Nika Taylor, Nicole Taylor was given "a more serious diagnosis" around nine months later.

"...After she asked the doctors her prognosis, [they said] it was around three months. And if the treatments worked, they didn't know how long [she had] after that," Nika Taylor said.

In response to that news, Natalie Taylor said her sister replied, "Everybody's gonna face judgment, and I'm ready to."

Born March 18, 1991, the Taylor sisters formed their music group Red Roots in 2010, releasing their self-titled debut studio album in 2011.

Their second studio album, "The Middle of Nowhere," was released in 2012, followed by their third studio album, "Triplicity," in 2014.

The trio signed with Inpop Records in 2015 and changed their name to Taylor Red, later releasing the track "Country Money" in 2021.

Nika and Natalie Taylor said throughout their sister's life, Nicole Taylor kept a deep and steady faith.

"We are still shocked and didn't think this would happen," Nika Taylor said in the Instagram video. "But we know she's not suffering anymore, and we have God's promise of ultimate healing."

articles.title: 'Grand Theft Auto' community organizing 'last ride' on old game before release of 'GTA VI,' but why?
articles.summary: The GTA community's "Last Ride" through Los Santos before "Grand Theft Auto VI" drops November 19 is trending, but the nostalgia may be overblown.
articles.body: November is finally upon us, and aside from setting our clocks back an hour, that also means we are a little more than two weeks away from the release of "Grand Theft Auto VI." The hotly anticipated title is set to drop on November 19, and the gaming community at large can hardly wait, which is understandable considering they've gone 13 years between installments. Yes, hard to believe that, as of September 17 of this year, "Grand Theft Auto V" would be old enough to see a PG-13 movie in theaters. UNKNOWN HACKER ALLEGEDLY LEAKS SEVERAL MINUTES OF GRAND THEFT AUTO VI GAMEPLAY AHEAD OF NETFLIX REVEAL Given the large time gap between games, you would expect there to be equal parts yearning for the new game as there is nostalgia for the old one, and from that nostalgia comes the "Last Ride." The "Last Ride" was pitched by the GTA community, and will see thousands of players take one last lap around the map of Los Santos — the in-game world for "GTA V" based heavily on Los Angeles — the night before "GTA VI's" big release. It's been trending heavily on social media, with gaming outlets all over the world picking up on it. As a particularly nostalgic person myself as well as a fan of the "Grand Theft Auto" series, I can see where these guys and gals are coming from with the "Last Ride," but it doesn't make a whole lot of sense when you peel the layers back a bit. For starters, "GTA V" isn't going anywhere. On November 20, you will still be able to pop the disc into your Xbox or Playstation and ride around Los Santos in your vehicle of choice to your heart's content. Hell, I still play "GTA IV" about as much as I play its predecessor, and I doubt I'll stop playing either once VI comes around. If you love the game that much, I guarantee you November 18 won't be the last time you ever play "GTA V." I appreciate the symbolism, but let's not get melodramatic here. When "Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask" came out, do you think everyone just immediately chucked their copies of "Ocarina of Time" in the trash? NINTENDO OF AMERICA RELEASES TEASER TRAILER CONFIRMING LEGEND OF ZELDA: OCARINA OF TIME REMAKE IN 2026 No, and as a matter of fact, the demand for "Ocarina of Time" has remained so high over the last 28 years that a remake is coming to the Nintendo Switch 2 later this month. This isn't "Madden" or "FIFA," where an updated version makes last year's game immediately obsolete. "GTA V" is unique because of the world the developers created as well as the memories those who played the game created for themselves. I'm not here to yuck anyone's yum; take the "Last Ride." Enjoy it. articles.standfirst: O VI Festival de Covers de Rio das Ostras acontece de 6 a 8 de novembro.
articles.summary: O VI Festival de Covers de Rio das Ostras acontece de 6 a 8 de novembro.
articles.body:
Três dias de shows, música e homenagens a grandes nomes nacionais e internacionais — Foto: Divulgação

Três dias de shows, música e homenagens a grandes nomes nacionais e internacionais marcam o VI Festival de Covers de Rio das Ostras, de 6 a 8 de novembro, na Lagoa do Iriry. Com entrada gratuita, o evento reúne bandas e artistas que recriam repertórios de diferentes gerações e estilos musicais. Durante o festival, haverá recolhimento de alimentos não perecíveis para doação a pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade. O público também contará com uma ampla praça de alimentação.

Entre os destaques estão o projeto Amy Reggaehouse, dedicado a Amy Winehouse; a banda Fever, com os sucessos do Aerosmith; e a Ciência de Chico, que homenageia Chico Science e Nação Zumbi, referências do movimento manguebeat. O cantor Valério Araújo também integra a programação com um tributo a Cazuza, interpretando canções que marcaram a trajetória do artista.

O festival se consolidou como uma potência cultural e econômica para Rio das Ostras. Em suas edições anteriores, reuniu mais de 300 mil pessoas, apresentou mais de 70 bandas e movimentou mais de R$ 4 milhões na economia local por edição. Os números refletem o alcance do evento e sua contribuição para setores como comércio, rede hoteleira e economia criativa.

Além de celebrar grandes referências da música, o festival abre espaço para os artistas da região. A iniciativa contribui para dar visibilidade às bandas locais e ampliar as oportunidades de apresentação para músicos que trabalham com tributos, fortalecendo a cena musical do município.

PROGRAMAÇÃO – Na sexta-feira, 6, a programação começa às 18h, com DJ. Às 20h, a banda Equalize apresenta um tributo à cantora Pitty. O encerramento da noite, às 22h30, fica por conta da Black Circle, com repertório dedicado ao Pearl Jam.

No sábado, 7, os shows começam às 13h, com a banda Durden, que interpreta músicas do Arctic Monkeys. Às 15h, a Markyze homenageia o Charlie Brown Jr. Na sequência, às 16h30, MKZ e Igor Carvalho apresentam um tributo ao O Rappa. Às 18h, o Rockstreet Boys sobe ao palco com um show dedicado às boy bands. A banda Fever se apresenta às 20h, com sucessos do Aerosmith, e, às 22h30, Amy Reggaehouse encerra a noite com músicas de Amy Winehouse.

No domingo, 8, a programação começa às 15h, com Cida Garcia interpretando canções de Alcione. Às 17h, a Ciência de Chico homenageia Chico Science e Nação Zumbi. Luan Schuenckel apresenta um especial dedicado a Lulu Santos às 19h. O encerramento do festival está previsto para as 21h, com Valério Araújo e seu tributo a Cazuza, o poeta exagerado.

REALIZAÇÃO – O VI Festival de Covers é realizado pela Fundação Rio das Ostras de Cultura, em correalização com a Associação de Arquitetos e Engenheiros de Rio das

Ostras. A produção é da TT Produções e Eventos. O evento conta com apoio institucional da Prefeitura de Rio das Ostras, da Câmara Municipal, do Experimente Rio das Ostras e do SAAE.

articles.title: Spencer Pratt says $1,200 hotel 'fortress' was cheaper than security as death threats mounted
articles.summary: Spencer Pratt says death threats and armed security costs during the Los Angeles mayoral race made the Hotel Bel-Air the cheapest option available.
articles.body: Spencer Pratt explained why his controversial stay at the Hotel Bel-Air was actually the cheaper option as he faced death threats while running for mayor of Los Angeles. The 43-year-old reality star faced scrutiny in May after TMZ reported he had been staying at the luxury hotel despite appearing to suggest in a campaign ad that he was living in an Airstream trailer on the site of his California home, which was destroyed in the devastating Pacific Palisades fire. At the time, the outlet reported that Pratt had been staying at the Hotel Bel-Air for more than a month, though "The Hills" alum disputed that characterization, saying he had spent no more than six days there during the previous month. SPENCER PRATT’S MAYORAL RUN BACKED BY PARIS HILTON, KRISTIN CAVALLARI AS CELEBRITY DIVIDE DEEPENS In a lengthy X post he shared Tuesday, Pratt, who lost in the June primary election, defended his choice to stay at the pricey hotel during the race. "Why is he spending $1,200 a night? Why couldn’t he stay somewhere for $300 a night? Well, the answer to that question is not as pretty as any of us may like to hear," Pratt wrote. REALITY TV STAR SPENCER PRATT GAINS TRACTION IN LOS ANGELES MAYORAL RACE AFTER FIERY DEBATE "Most people simply presumed that I was being a bougie spoiled brat, and that I was abusing campaign funds," he continued. "They expected me to stay at a cheaper hotel, but what they don’t realize is … the Hotel Bel Air was the cheapest hotel in all of LA. "At the time, I couldn’t explain the math to people, and my campaign staff told me I wasn’t allowed to divulge the real reason I had to stay there, but now that the election is coming to a close, I don’t need to listen to anyone anymore." 'ENTOURAGE' CREATOR BACKS SPENCER PRATT FOR LA MAYOR, SAYS CITY 'HAS COLLAPSED' UNDER CURRENT LEADERSHIP Pratt had previously told TMZ in May that the Airstream had become unsafe, saying that the Bel Air Hotel's "armed security" made it "the only option." He claimed that supporters of his opponents, Mayor Karen Bass and City Councilmember Nithya Raman were "getting increasingly desperate and hostile" due to his performance at the May debate and strong polling numbers. "I can't talk about specific threats, but that lot is ... unsafe now," he said at the time. JIMMY KIMMEL ATTACKS FIRE VICTIM SPENCER PRATT AS 'SCREAMING JERK,' LECTURES LA VOTERS ABOUT MAYORAL ELECTION In his X post, Pratt, who ran as a Republican, elaborated on the threats that he received, which he attributed to political violence. "Throughout the campaign, I endured numerous death threats, to the point where I had to hire full-time security," he wrote. "Anyone who’s had to hire security knows that they will always tell you to not discuss your death threats; they find that it often has the opposite effect you would expect; normal people should hear it and think ‘whoa, we need to dial back the temperature, this isn’t acceptable’, but the reality is that commie street animals get inspired, and you will end up getting copycats if you advertise your threats." SPENCER PRATT VOWS TO LEAVE LA AND FIND 'LAST AMERICAN DREAM' IN ANOTHER CITY IF MAYORAL BID FAILS Pratt went on to detail specific incidents he said led him to fear for his safety and that of his family. "People were breaking into my lot in the Palisades and leaving notes on the airstream with white powder in them," he wrote. DEM MAYOR FACES REALITY CHECK AFTER ACCUSING RIVAL OF 'EXPLOITING' PALISADES FIRE: 'ABSOLUTE TONE DEAFNESS' The TV personality also claimed that a "lunatic" who was "hellbent on tracking me down" charged at his young son while he was boogie-boarding in the ocean. Pratt shares sons Gunner, 8, and Ryker, 3, with his wife and former "The Hills" co-star Heidi Montag, 40. "So, I had to hire a second security detail for my family while I was away campaigning," he wrote. "I don’t know if you’ve ever had to hire 4-5 armed security professionals with blacked out SUVs, but…it’s not cheap. One of the first things they told me was that my lot in the Palisades was a security nightmare; perched mid-slope on a hill, totally exposed in a bowl, surrounded by elevated positions where a shooter could easily traipse through the wilderness of the State Park, and have a clear line of sight to every inch of my property. SPENCER PRATT: LOS ANGELES ANGRY WITH KAREN BASS’ MISMANAGEMENT "I wasn’t allowed to stay on that property, even if I wanted to," he added. "Enter the Hotel Bel Air." Pratt explained that the famed LA hotel, which has hosted celebrities, presidents and royalty, is an unusually secure property due to its design. PRATT CONCEDES LA MAYOR RACE WITH SCATHING VIDEO TEASING NEXT MOVE, BOMBSHELL INFO HE HOLDS: 'COMMIE ANIMALS' "While $1,200 a night isn’t very unique for a decent hotel in a major city, there’s something else about the hotel that is unique," Pratt wrote. "Unlike my turkey shoot of a lot in the Palisades, the Hotel Bel Air is surrounded with a fortress wall, with a single point of ingress, a fatal funnel that takes you over a moat, just to enter the property. You then must navigate a labyrinth of walled off bungalows, and it is very easy to get lost. Unlike normal hotels, it is a very secure facility. "When my security team dropped me off behind the walls of the Bel Air, they felt good about leaving me alone in the secure facility," he continued. "Had I stayed anywhere else, I would have needed to book out 3 rooms for my team to maintain overnight security, which would’ve cost an additional $3,000 per night. Paradoxically, by this calculation, I was actually saving a ton of money by staying at the secure Bel Air; even staying at a Motel 6 would’ve cost me more money, and in a campaign…money is everything." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Pratt claimed that threats of political violence disproportionately affect Republican candidates, arguing that the cost of protecting himself forced his campaign to spend money on security that his Democratic rivals could devote elsewhere. The reality star recalled that Raman appeared at a debate preparation event without visible security while he was accompanied by several armed officers. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? "I knew that I needed armed security, and even though it severely crippled our campaign by siphoning off an insane amount of our fundraising dollars, we had to do it, because we knew that nobody else was going to protect us." articles.title: Swedish Ambassador Petra Menander: Diwali is already my favourite time of the year in India
articles.summary: This is Swedish Ambassador Petra Menander's first Diwali in India, and the festival has already become her favourite time of the year.
articles.body: This is Swedish Ambassador Petra Menander's first Diwali in India, and the festival has already become her favourite time of the year. While shopping for earthen diyas and painting a few of them at SN's Matka Market, she tells us jokingly, "This can be my second career. I am genuinely enjoying painting these diyas."Thanking the shopkeepers with a 'dhanyavad' and greeting them with a 'namaste', Ambassador Petra Menander walks through the market lanes dressed in her festive best.She tells us that she is looking forward to celebrating her first Diwali in India. "There is something wonderful about a festival that transforms homes, streets, markets and entire cities with light, colour and celebrations. It is interesting to see how families and friends come together and experience the warmth of Indian hospitality. My visit to Matka Market in Sarojini Nagar, Delhi, has made the excitement even more real. I picked up earthen diyas, bandhanwars and other festive decorations to bring a little Diwali magic into my home. It was lovely to see how much thought and creativity go into preparing for the festival," says the ambassador.She also shares that she has a keen interest in textiles and sustainable fabrics, thanks to her grandmother. "I am always drawn to traditional crafts and the stories behind them. While painting diyas at the market, I realised that pottery may be the next skill I would like to learn! It gave me a new appreciation for the artistry and hard work of local artisans. I was also struck by how the use of earthen diyas reflects a connection to both tradition and sustainability, values that are close to Sweden’s heart as well," she tells us.Talking about the celebrations at the Embassy, the ambassador shares that they will celebrate together with colleagues by decorating the premises with rangoli and marigold flowers, lighting diyas and, of course, enjoying some Indian food."What strikes me most is that Diwali is about so much more than lights and decorations. You can feel the excitement and anticipation everywhere - in the streets, in the markets and in people's homes. There is a sense of joy and festivity in the air. One thing I particularly appreciate is how Diwali brings families and friends together. The emphasis on reconnecting, sharing happiness and making time for loved ones is something I find very meaningful. As someone living in India, I have come to appreciate this warmth and sense of community, and it is lovely to experience it first-hand."The ambassador points out that Lucia is a Swedish festival that shares similarities with Diwali."Growing up in Sweden, Lucia was a reminder that even in the darkest winter, light returns, symbolising the triumph of light over darkness. Experiencing Diwali in India, I see a similar message expressed in a different and much grander way. In many ways, there is a beautiful parallel with Diwali - the idea that light brings hope and a sense of togetherness.Sweden’s Lucia tradition is celebrated in December, during the darkest time of the year. Children and adults dress in white, carry candles and sing together, bringing light and warmth into the winter darkness. For me, Diwali also reflects values that are important to Sweden, including sustainability and a close connection to tradition. Across India, many families continue to light earthen diyas made from natural materials by local artisans. It is a beautiful example of how cultural heritage can go hand in hand with sustainability and support local communities," she says and adds that they also celebrate Midsummer, when families and friends gather outdoors to welcome the longest days of the year."It is a joyful celebration of nature, food, music and community. The traditions may look different, but the sentiment is similar - whether it is lighting a diya in India or a candle in Sweden," she explains.Cultural celebrations like Diwali play a role in strengthening our strategic partnership. "It is wonderful to see how Diwali has become a part of Sweden’s cultural landscape. The Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs and Sweden’s Prime Minister have extended Diwali greetings to people in India, reflecting the importance Sweden attaches to its relationship with India. Across Sweden, various cultural organisations host local Diwali melas (fairs), music concerts and community dinners that bring together people from diverse backgrounds. These celebrations help bring India and Sweden closer," she says.As she heads back to the Embassy with her diyas and other Diwali purchases, she tells us, "Diwali is already my favourite time of the year in India. As Sweden’s Ambassador to India, I am deeply touched by the warmth and beauty of this festival, the glow of diyas, the sharing of sweets and the coming together of families and communities. My warmest wishes to everyone in India for a very happy Diwali! May this Diwali strengthen the friendship between Sweden and India. Dil se Deepawali ki shubhkamnayein!"Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Military heritage is not nostalgia. It is a strategic advantage.
articles.summary: India’s military history is not merely a record of wars fought and victories won.
articles.body: India’s military history is not merely a record of wars fought and victories won. It is also a story of institutional evolution, strategic adaptation and the lessons that continue to shape the country’s defence preparedness. This larger perspective came into focus at the fourth edition of the Indian Military Heritage Festival (IMHF) 2026, which concluded in New Delhi on October 31, bringing together military leadership, veterans, historians, authors, academics and strategic affairs experts for two days of discussions on India’s military past and its future security challenges.Organised by the United Service Institution of India’s (USI) Centre for Military History and Conflict Studies (CMHCS) on October 30–31, the festival sought to take military history beyond specialist circles and bring it into wider public conversation. Its programme combined panel discussions, book launches, a tri-service exhibition, special addresses and conversations on military heritage, operational experience, technology, jointmanship and the human cost of conflict.The festival’s opening address by Vice Admiral Sanjay Jasjit Singh (Indian Navy, Retd), Director General, USI, reflected the institution’s commitment to preserving and sharing India’s military heritage. He noted that what began as the first edition of the festival in 2023 had grown into a signature event of the institution.“Good day to all the historians, distinguished guests and academicians. What began as the first edition of the Indian Military Heritage Festival in 2023 has, over the years, grown into a signature event of the United Service Institution of India. USI has a rich institutional legacy, supported by a library of around 72,000 books and an extensive archive of historical records. Among its prized archival holdings is an original copy of the document relating to the 1971 surrender. These resources reflect the Institution’s commitment to preserving India’s military history and making it accessible to future generations,” Vice Admiral Singh said.The archival reference was particularly significant. Military history is often remembered through major battles and public commemorations, but original documents, institutional records and personal accounts provide evidence through which these events can be examined, understood and passed on to future generations.The festival opened with a special session on the military history of the Garhwal Rifles, featuring Lieutenant General Syed Ata Hasnain, Governor of Bihar; other eminences; and Lieutenant General Dinesh Rana, among others. The programme also explored the contributions of the Garhwal Rifles in Operation Pawan, the history of the Corps of Engineers, Operation Safed Sagar during the 1999 Kargil conflict and the Indian Army’s wars between 1947 and 1999.Other sessions brought forward dimensions of military history that are often less visible in conventional accounts of warfare. These included the shared military heritage of India and Britain, the experiences of soldiers’ families, military medicine and the role of doctors in conflict. A conversation on women officers who participated in India’s global sailing expeditions, Samudra Pradakshina and Navika Sagar Parikrama, also highlighted changing opportunities and contributions across the three services.The maritime dimension received particular attention on the festival’s second day, with Indian Navy veteran and naval historian Commodore (Dr) Srikant B. Kesnur (Retd) playing a central role. He moderated two important sessions that connected the Navy’s historical journey with its present-day technological and strategic priorities.The first, titled ‘Indian Navy’s Indigenization Journey – Past, Present, and Future’, brought together Vice Admiral B Sivakumar, Chief of Materiel; Rear Admiral Sujit Baxi, Director General, Warship Design Bureau; Captain (IN) N S Mohan Ram (Retd); Commodore Arun P Golaya (Retd); and Commodore Pramod R Kulkarni (Retd). The discussion examined the Navy’s transition from dependence on foreign suppliers towards indigenous ship design, domestic production and closer partnerships with Indian industry.The central question was not simply how many warships India can build, but how effectively the country can design, develop, maintain and upgrade the technologies that sustain its maritime strength. The session reflected the growing importance of Aatmanirbharta in securing supply chains, supporting distant deployments and strengthening India’s ability to operate as a first responder in the Indian Ocean region.Cmdre. Kesnur also moderated the session ‘1946–1971: Uprising to Risen’, which traced two defining moments in the evolution of Indian naval power. The discussion brought together Vice Admiral Anup Singh (Retd), Commander Vipin Sharma (Retd), maritime historian Swaroop Anand and defence journalist Sandeep Unnithan. It examined the 1946 Royal Indian Navy uprising, when Indian ratings challenged colonial authority, and the Indian Navy’s decisive missile-boat operations against Karachi during the 1971 India-Pakistan War. Together, the two episodes offered a perspective on the Navy’s journey from the final years of colonial rule to the emergence of a more confident maritime force.The sessions acquired an additional dimension with the release of Cmdre. Kesnur’s book, The War in the Indian Ocean, published by Sabre and Quill. The book was among the three naval titles released during the festival’s Future Ready Navy segment, alongside Captain (IN) N S Mohan Ram’s A Builder’s Navy: The Long Road to Self-sufficiency in Warship Design and Commodore Pramod R Kulkarni’s Warship Design and its Management: A Systems Engineering Perspective. The releases brought together naval history, indigenous shipbuilding and the technical management of warship design—three subjects closely linked to India’s evolving maritime ambitions.The wider strategic context was articulated by Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan in his address during the Future Ready Navy session. He placed the maritime domain at the centre of India’s economic growth, national security and strategic interests, underlining the country’s dependence on seaborne trade and the importance of protecting maritime routes and critical infrastructure as India moves towards Viksit Bharat 2047.The CNS identified four major changes shaping the maritime environment: intensifying strategic competition around shipping routes and chokepoints; the growing influence of non-state actors and commercial entities; the expansion of the maritime domain from the seabed to outer space, accompanied by greater surveillance and transparency; and the wider availability of advanced technologies such as drones, artificial intelligence and satellite imagery.His larger point was that disruptions at sea do not remain confined to the oceans. They can affect energy supplies, food and fertiliser availability, trade and supply chains, with consequences that eventually reach households and businesses on land. For a country with extensive maritime interests, this makes naval preparedness an essential part of economic and national security.Admiral Swaminathan also outlined the Navy’s response: modernising its force, reviewing operational doctrines and strengthening indigenous technological and industrial capabilities. He emphasised that conventional naval platforms would continue to provide the foundation of maritime power, while unmanned and autonomous systems would add flexibility and scale. Self-reliance, he said, must extend beyond manufacturing to the ability to design, maintain, repair and upgrade critical systems domestically.An important aspect of his address was the need to prepare for operations in environments where satellite-based positioning, navigation and timing services could be disrupted. While the Navy is working towards greater use of NavIC as the system matures, it is also developing alternative capabilities to remain effective in GPS- and satellite-based PNT-denied environments. This reflects a broader military requirement: the ability to continue operating when technologies and services that are normally taken for granted become unavailable.The festival’s other discussions reinforced the idea that military history must inform present-day thinking. Sessions on the Indian Air Force’s role in Operation Safed Sagar, the integration of princely-state forces into the national military after Independence, institutionalizing jointmanship through HQ IDS and the Andaman and Nicobar Command, and the experiences of women officers all offered different perspectives on how India’s Armed Forces have evolved.The two-day event also featured a tri-service exhibition showcasing the histories and contributions of the Army, Navy and Air Force, with a special focus on the Garhwal Rifles. Book releases and discussions provided a platform for military professionals and researchers to bring archival material, operational experience and personal narratives into public discourse.Ultimately, the fourth edition of IMHF made a case for treating military heritage as a living national resource. The value of studying the 1946 naval uprising, the 1971 operations, the Kargil conflict or the evolution of indigenous warship design lies not only in remembering what happened, but in understanding how institutions adapt to changing strategic circumstances.As the CNS observed, the Navy must continuously recognize emerging trends and prepare for an uncertain future. The festival brought that thought into sharper focus: a nation that understands its military past is better placed to make informed choices about its defence future. By connecting history with technology, operational experience and strategic debate, IMHF 2026 offered a platform to do precisely that.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.

articles.title: Kanika Kapoor announces separation from husband Gautam Hathiramani after four years of marriage: 'This is my second time for a divorce and that brings its own grief and disappointment'
articles.summary: Singer Kanika Kapoor has announced that she and her husband, Gautam Hathiramani, have decided to part ways.
articles.body: Singer Kanika Kapoor has announced that she and her husband, Gautam Hathiramani, have decided to part ways. The ‘Baby Doll’ singer shared the news through an Instagram story on Tuesday, requesting privacy as they navigate the separation. The announcement came a day after she removed their wedding photographs from her social media account. Kanika, 48, married Gautam in an intimate ceremony in London in May 2022.Sharing a statement about their decision, Kanika wrote, “Dear friends and family, after much thought and consideration, my husband and I are going our separate ways. I am grateful for the time we shared and wish him well for the future. I sincerely ask for kindness and respect for our privacy as we move forward. Love, Kanika.”In an interview with Mumbai Mirror, the singer addressed speculation surrounding the split, clarifying that neither of them had found someone else. She also dismissed reports suggesting that she was unwilling to relocate to Lagos, where Gautam is based professionally. According to the publication, some of Gautam’s friends claimed that he was deeply affected by the separation. They reportedly attributed the growing differences to Kanika’s frequent travel for live performances and demanding work commitments, which they said made it difficult for Gautam to manage his professional responsibilities in Lagos.Addressing these claims, Kanika told the publication, “I have not found anybody else, and to the best of my knowledge, neither has Gautam. For me, this is my second time for a divorce and that brings its own grief and disappointment. To say that I did not want to stay in Lagos is not true, and it’s so typical – that when a marriage falls apart, the first person to be blamed is the woman – which is unfair. Only two people in a marriage know what exactly transpires between them. I have three children that I need to take care of. I hope to keep my future interactions with Gautam amicable, as I am not an aggressive person. I think he would wish the same.”Kanika and Gautam reportedly shared a friendship spanning nearly 15 years before they decided to get married. The singer is said to have proposed to him twice, first in 2014 and again in 2020. Gautam eventually proposed in 2021, and the two tied the knot the following year. Their wedding was an intimate affair attended by close friends and family, with Kanika’s three children also taking part in the celebrations.This was Kanika’s second marriage. She was previously married to London-based NRI general practitioner Raj Chandok, also known as Dr Jaspreet Singh Chandok, in 1998. The couple have three children together: daughters Aayana and Samara, and son Yuvraaj. They divorced in 2012, following which Kanika moved to India.On the professional front, Kanika made her mark with ‘Jugni Ji’ in 2012 before becoming a recognised playback singer in the Hindi film industry. Her career took off with ‘Baby Doll’ from ‘Ragini MMS 2’, which became a major hit in 2014. She also earned popularity for ‘Chittiyan Kalaiyaan’ from ‘Roy’ that year. Some of her other notable tracks include ‘Tukur Tukur’ from Shah Rukh Khan’s ‘Dilwale’ and the Hindi version of ‘Oo Antava’ from ‘Pushpa: The Rise’, which she recorded in 2021. articles.title: Regina Cassandra says female stars deserve grand cutouts like male superstars, praises her 'Mookuthi Amman 2' co-star Nayanthara
articles.summary: Actress Regina Cassandra has opened up about her experience of playing a negative role in Sundar C's 'Mookuthi Amman 2'.
articles.body: Actress Regina Cassandra has opened up about her experience of playing a negative role in Sundar C's 'Mookuthi Amman 2'. The actress said the film gave her an opportunity to explore a different kind of character in a big commercial project. She also spoke about the extensive use of visual effects, her challenging makeup sessions, and the effort that went into creating her look. Regina Cassandra, who was last seen in Ajith Kumar's 'Vidaamuyarchi', said she enjoyed working on the fantasy entertainer and was excited about the final result.3,000 VFX shots and two-hour makeup sessions in 'Mookuthi Amman 2'Speaking about her role in an interview with Cinema Vikatan, Regina Cassandra said, "For the first time in my career, I have played a villain in such a big commercial film. I enjoyed every moment of it, both technically and emotionally. The audience will also get a similar experience while watching the film. Most of the scenes and shots featuring me have a lot of graphics. As director Sundar C sir mentioned, the film has at least 3,000 CGI shots. A large team has been working on the visual effects for the past year." She added that her makeup alone took around two hours every day. Recalling her introduction scene, she said, "They poured a sticky liquid made of honey and pistachio green colour over me, from head to toe. Managing that and performing the scene was a different experience altogether."Regina Cassandra praises Nayanthara's 60-foot cutout and calls it a positive changeRegina also shared her thoughts on the 60-foot cutout erected for Nayanthara ahead of the film's release. She said such grand celebrations were usually associated with leading male stars in Tamil cinema. "For several decades, we have seen huge cutouts being put up only for male superstars. We have rarely seen the same for actresses. Only after Nayanthara's cutout was installed did I learn that Radhika ma'am had also received one for 'Thaai Kizhavi'. She has been achieving so much in the film industry for over 30 to 40 years, and this recognition has come now. Seeing actresses like Nayanthara and Radhika receive such grand cutouts, just like male actors, is a healthy change in the industry," she said.On villain roles after Ajith Kumar's 'Vidaamuyarchi'The actress also spoke about the kind of roles coming her way after 'Vidaamuyarchi'. Regina said she has received several offers to play negative characters following the Ajith Kumar-starrer. However, she does not want to be limited to one type of role. "After working in a big film like 'Vidaamuyarchi' with Ajith sir, it is easy for the industry to place an actor in a particular category and offer similar roles. I am very clear that I do not want that to happen to me. That is why I am careful about the films I choose and prefer to work on a limited number of projects," she said.Directed by Sundar C, 'Mookuthi Amman 2', featuring Nayanthara, Urvashi and Regina, is scheduled for a Diwali release.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Exclusive! Saumya Tandon: I consider myself a struggler for life
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview, actress Saumya Tandon reflects on her evolving career post-Dhurandhar, her challenges in finding quality scripts, and her determination to continue growing as an artist in the competitive film industry.
articles.body: Sometimes, a small role can make a big impact, and Saumya Tandon has experienced that with Dhurandhar. Known for her comic performances, the actress surprised audiences with a layered, intense portrayal that relied on expressions and silences rather than dialogue. The film has brought her a new wave of recognition. While the appreciation has been reassuring, have the right opportunities come as easily as she would have hoped? As she moves on to a very different character in a Sooraj Barjatya’s next, Saumya reflects on life after Dhurandhar, the struggle to find quality scripts and her determination to keep evolving as an actor.‘Things have taken off post Dhurandhar’Talking about life post Dhurandhar, Saumya says, “Things have taken off post Dhurandhar. I think there is a lot of validation from people in the industry now. I always thought I could, but now even they feel that I can do something serious and deep which has a lot of layers. I get a lot of calls from people saying, ‘Oh, you act so well.’ I was always seen as somebody who did comedy and had not done anything intense like this before. So, there has been a change.”‘The struggle is to find the right character in a good script’Saumya is excited about her part in Sooraj Barjatya’s upcoming release, however, she explains that actors often find themselves being offered variations of characters they have already played. “They tend to keep calling you for similar parts — a wife grieving the loss of a child or a complicated husband-wife relationship. The struggle is to find the right character in a good script. The real challenge in this industry is finding a good script and a good part. I have always been a thinking actor, and I have always struggled. I consider myself a struggler for life. If you are looking for quality work and good parts, it is going to be tough because there are very few good scripts.”‘With time, I have calmed down’Saumya admits that her career has not unfolded quite as she had imagined when she first arrived in Mumbai. “When I came to Mumbai and started out, I had huge expectations of myself. I really thought I would star as a leading lady in Bollywood. So yes, I am definitely failing at that. Having said that, I think I am on a journey. With time and so many years in this industry, I have calmed down. I feel the focus should be on how you are evolving and improving as an artiste, rather than just looking at where you have reached.”‘I don’t expect anything from this industry’The increased recognition has not necessarily translated into the kind of work she has been hoping for. Saumya believes that finding a good script and a character that offers something new remains the real challenge. “A lot has happened, but I am a little disappointed that a lot more could have happened and has not. I don’t expect anything from this industry. I am pretty cynical about it. I don’t think the industry really roots for you or changes things for you. You have to change things for yourself. The calls have increased, and the roles being offered are more now, but the question is: what kind of roles are coming my way? They should be different from what I have already done.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Brundle unconvinced Ferrari can stop another Hamilton-Leclerc clash
articles.summary: Martin Brundle expects another flashpoint between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, warning that any internal talks within Ferrari following their clash in...
articles.body:
Martin Brundle expects another flashpoint between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc , warning that any internal talks within Ferrari following their clash in Mexico are unlikely to prevent a repeat.

Ferrari missed out on a potential 1-2 after both drivers ran wide at Turn 4, when Leclerc challenged Hamilton for the lead. Max Verstappen capitalised to take the victory, with Hamilton finishing in P2 and Leclerc in P4.

Brundle expects Ferrari to address the clash internally before this weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix. However, he questioned whether any meeting would prevent a repeat situation between their two drivers.

He told Sky Sports:"it doesn't look pretty for the team, it's like when Lando (Norris) ran into Oscar Piastri in Singapore in the sprint race, it doesn't look pretty for the team and you let 1,500 people down and that's just the car side. You let people down in your team, you are only the final link in the chain of your team but you are the one out there that's got to deliver in the heat of the moment.

"So Ferrari will have to manage that somehow and they will sit down, we will go to Brazil, and they will say 'yes we've sat down and we understood it all, move forward, it won't happen again,' but in reality we know that it will.

Brundle: Leclerc has had frustrations this year

Brundle also told Sky Sports that there has been some frustration within the Ferrari camp this season, particularly on Leclerc's side. After dominating Hamilton in 2025, Leclerc, until now, has been outperformed more often than not by the seven-time world champion.

Despite Hamilton's criticism of Leclerc after the Mexico City Grand Prix, Brundle defended Leclerc, with a reference to Ayrton Senna's famous quote about not going for a gap which is there.

He said: "You know what? They're hardwired racing drivers. It's a curious business we have where you perform as an individual totally in a team environment. You're measured as an individual, you're rewarded as an individual.

"And then when the adrenaline's up and the chance of the gap is there, as the great Ayrton Senna said, 'If you don't go for a gap, you're no longer a racing driver.' And that's what they did. There's some frustration. Charles had some frustrations this year."

articles.title: Alberto Angela reconstruye la conquista de la Galia y descubre al hombre detrás del mito de Julio César en 'César. La conquista de la eternidad'
articles.standfirst: El divulgador italiano combina historia y arqueología para reconstruir las campañas militares del general romano y descubrir al hombre detrás de uno de los grandes mitos de la Antigüedad
articles.summary: El divulgador italiano combina historia y arqueología para reconstruir las campañas militares del general romano y descubrir al hombre detrás de uno de los grandes mitos de la Antigüedad
articles.body: En el año 58 a. C., Julio César abandonó Roma al frente de sus legiones para emprender la conquista de la Galia. Durante ocho años protagonizó una de las mayores campañas militares de la Antigüedad, con batallas sangrientas, expediciones a Britania, incursiones más allá del Rin y enfrentamientos con pueblos que resistieron el avance romano. Una aventura que cambiaría el equilibrio de poder en Roma y dejaría una huella decisiva en la historia europea. Esa es la historia que reconstruye el paleontólogo, naturalista y divulgador italiano Alberto Angela en 'César. La conquista de la eternidad', publicado en España por La Esfera de los Libros. La obra, que llegó a las librerías italianas de la mano de Mondadori en noviembre de 2025 y se convirtió en número uno de ventas, recupera el relato de 'De bello Gallico', la obra en la que el propio César narró sus campañas militares, para ofrecer una nueva mirada sobre uno de los personajes más fascinantes de la historia. Alberto Angela combina el testimonio de César con los conocimientos actuales de arqueología, antropología, historia y geografía, con el propósito de contrastar la versión del vencedor y reconstruir tanto los acontecimientos militares como el contexto político y social de aquella época. "Llevaba 30 años queriendo escribir este libro", reconoce el autor, que se propuso abordar 'De bello Gallico' desde una perspectiva científica e histórica y recuperar una obra que nació como una recopilación de informes militares destinados al Senado romano. El resultado va más allá de una biografía convencional y convierte la conquista de la Galia en un relato de aventuras, exploración, guerra y poder, sin renunciar al rigor de la divulgación histórica. El recorrido abarca los principales episodios de las campañas desarrolladas entre el 58 y el 50 a. C.: los enfrentamientos con los helvecios y los germanos, la guerra contra los belgas, la batalla naval contra los vénetos, las expediciones a Britania y al otro lado del Rin, las rebeliones galas y el enfrentamiento definitivo con Vercingétorix en Alesia. El libro se detiene también en aspectos menos conocidos de la vida militar romana, como la organización de las legiones, la construcción de los campamentos, las armas utilizadas por los soldados y las costumbres de los pueblos galos y sus druidas. Sin embargo, la conquista de la Galia no fue únicamente una sucesión de victorias militares. Alberto Angela muestra cómo César libraba dos guerras al mismo tiempo: una en los territorios que pretendía someter y otra en Roma, donde las rivalidades políticas, el Triunvirato y la progresiva crisis de la República condicionaban sus decisiones. Aquellos años fueron determinantes para su transformación en un dirigente capaz de alterar el sistema político romano y acelerar el final de la República. El retrato que propone Alberto Angela también se aleja del héroe idealizado para mostrar a un hombre lleno de contradicciones. César fue un estratega implacable, un político brillante y un escritor excepcional, pero también un hombre con pasiones, ambiciones, miedos y dudas. Su extraordinaria capacidad para construir su propia imagen pública ocupa un lugar destacado en el libro. Consciente de la importancia de resultar reconocible ante sus soldados, cuidaba su apariencia incluso en el campo de batalla y aspiraba a convertirse en el Alejandro Magno del mundo romano. La narración tampoco esquiva las consecuencias más oscuras de sus campañas. Las matanzas ordenadas por César, la violencia de la conquista y el coste humano de las victorias romanas forman parte de una reflexión sobre la ética de la guerra y la manera de juzgar desde el presente acontecimientos que hoy podrían considerarse crímenes contra la humanidad. El autor plantea así una lectura que no se limita a ensalzar el genio militar del general, sino que también examina las consecuencias de su ambición y su ejercicio del poder. El título, 'César. La conquista de la eternidad', alude precisamente a la doble dimensión de aquella empresa. Además de conquistar territorios, César consiguió convertirse en uno de los personajes destinados a permanecer en la memoria colectiva. La romanización de la Galia dejó una profunda huella cultural y geopolítica que contribuyó a configurar la Europa posterior y cuyas consecuencias siguen siendo relevantes para comprender las raíces de Occidente. Alberto Angela resume el sentido de su obra con una idea: "Este es un libro sobre la guerra contra la guerra". El conocimiento de los conflictos del pasado sirve así para reflexionar sobre la ambición, el poder, la destrucción y el valor de la paz, en un momento en el que los enfrentamientos armados vuelven a ocupar un lugar central en la actualidad internacional. El proyecto incorpora, además, reconstrucciones de rostros, batallas y escenas de la vida cotidiana realizadas con ayuda de inteligencia artificial y guiadas por la investigación histórico-científica. Entre ellas destaca la recreación del rostro de Julio César, utilizada para la portada, las ilustraciones interiores y el material audiovisual de presentación del libro. Alberto Angela es uno de los divulgadores históricos y científicos más reconocidos de Italia. Paleontólogo y naturalista, ha desarrollado buena parte de su trayectoria en la investigación y la comunicación científica, además de presentar numerosos programas de éxito en la televisión pública italiana (RAI). Autor de libros traducidos a distintos idiomas, ya había publicado en La Esfera de los Libros 'Un día en la antigua Roma' y 'Amor y sexo en la antigua Roma'.

articles.body: The Mumbai Police have arrested a man accused of sending threatening messages to several Bollywood celebrities, including Ayushmann Khurrana and Tusshar Kapoor. The accused, Vaibhav Mishra, was reportedly posing as a member of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.Accused posed as a gang memberAccording to the IANS report, Vaibhav Mishra, who works as an IT engineer, was arrested in Bengaluru on Wednesday. He allegedly sent threatening audio messages to film personalities in the name of Lawrence Bishnoi. According to Mumbai Police sources, he had been targeting several celebrities living in Mumbai over the past few days.Ayushmann Khurrana and Tusshar Kapoor among those targetedAyushmann Khurrana reportedly received a threatening audio message from someone claiming links with the Bishnoi gang. The sender allegedly demanded crores of rupees from the ‘Dream Girl’ actor.Earlier, Tusshar Kapoor also reportedly received a similar audio message. The sender claimed to be Harry Boxxer, a member of the gang, and demanded Rs 5 crore from the ‘Golmaal’ actor. However, the preliminary investigation suggested the audio might be fake.Tiger Shroff firing case adds to concernsMeanwhile, the film industry was recently shaken by the firing attack on actor Tiger Shroff on October 18. The Lawrence Bishnoi group claimed responsibility for the attack.A representative of the group, Anil Pandit, posted on social media that they would not spare anyone who chooses to work closely with Salman Khan. He also released an audio clip asking Salman to apologise. In the clip, he said, “Listen to me carefully, Salman Khan. If you don’t apologise to my elder brother, Lawrence Bishnoi, or to the Bishnoi community, then we won’t even leave a dog in your house. We will destroy your entire family. Keep this in mind.
